questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic is about to merge from the right. Be ready to let that traffic merge safely.

questions.question: What does it mean when a school bus has flashing amber lights?

options.text: The bus just finished loading or unloading children.
The bus is about to stop to load or unload children. Get ready to stop.
The bus is broken down on the road and you should pass slowly.
The bus is loading or unloading children and you may go slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus is about to stop to load or unload children. Get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Flashing amber lights warn you that the bus will stop soon to load or unload children. Get ready to stop. When the red lights flash, stop before reaching the bus and stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other cars.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your car will need more time to stop.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the road means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other cars from your direction.

questions.question: As a driver, you must stop for a pedestrian crossing at:

options.text: Only marked crosswalks.
Both marked and unmarked crosswalks.
Only if the pedestrian is directly in front of your car.
Only if there is a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both marked and unmarked crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop for pedestrians crossing at any marked or unmarked crosswalk. Let them cross safely before you go.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to slow down, look both ways, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:

options.text: Make no driving errors.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it hard to stay in your lane and control your car.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads with a divider between them. Stay on the right side.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A steady red light means stop. You must come to a complete stop. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if no sign says otherwise.

questions.question: Drowsy drivers:

options.text: Should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
Can drive as badly as a drunk driver.
Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
Are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can drive as badly as a drunk driver.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive as badly as drunk drivers. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.
questions.explanation: Special child seats exist for small children. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always secure children properly in a seat before driving.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. If you see a yellow light, slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: To make a right turn, position your car:

options.text: In the center of the street.
On the left side of the street.
On the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across other lanes of traffic when turning.

questions.question: If you are in an accident and another person is injured, you should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Avoid moving them. Keep them warm and give first aid if you can.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid moving them. Keep them warm and give first aid if you can.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary. Moving them incorrectly can make small injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Look through the rear window as you back up. Do not depend only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Conditions are not perfect in any way.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions are not perfect in any way.
questions.explanation: Drive below the posted speed limit when roads are wet, visibility is poor, or any other condition is not ideal. Even if you are driving at the posted speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when one driver does not see another vehicle or when a driver does something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right.
Slow down and use your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is the driver's responsibility to watch for pedestrians and yield to them, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly if a tire blows out. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slowly release the gas pedal to reduce speed. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When can you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: What type of sign is diamond-shaped?

options.text: Road hazard sign.
Interstate route sign.
School crossing sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow (or orange in work areas). They warn you of hazards or special rules ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
A pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or near the roadway ahead. Drive carefully through the work zone.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your car and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycles is true?

options.text: Other drivers can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to come on when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns of a steep hill so you can adjust your speed safely.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related car crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Tell people "No thanks, I'm driving" if they offer you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: Decide before drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices after drinking.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before passing. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into the lane only when you can see the other car in your rearview mirror.
